nodes.label: Bail
nodes.summary: Right to bail, statutory exceptions, factors, bail pending appeal, variation/revocation, police/ICAC bail.

nodes.label: Right to Bail and Statutory Exceptions
nodes.summary: Presumption: accused has right to bail under Cap 221 s.9D(1). Exceptions (s.9D(2)): substantial grounds to believe accused would: (a) fail to surrender; (b) commit offence while on bail; (c) interfere with witnesses or pervert course of justice. Additional NSL exception: Art.42 NSL — bail shall not be granted unless judge satisfied no risk of national security danger.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.9D
nodes.summary: Right to bail (s.9D(1)) and statutory exceptions for refusal (s.9D(2)).

nodes.label: National Security Law Article 42
nodes.summary: Bail shall not be granted unless judge satisfied no risk of national security danger.

nodes.label: Factors in Bail Decisions
nodes.summary: Risk of absconding: nature/gravity of offence, strength of evidence, community ties, previous bail record, financial resources. Risk of reoffending: past convictions, nature of alleged offence, employment, family. Interference with witnesses: relationship to complainant, nature of threats. Surety and recognizance: court may require surety (cash deposit) and/or recognizance; amount must be proportionate.

nodes.label: Bail Pending Appeal
nodes.summary: Cap 221 s.9K: appeal against conviction/sentence does not automatically confer bail; special test — must not be in interests of justice. CFA bail pending appeal: under Cap 484 s.35; exceptional; high threshold.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.9K
nodes.summary: Bail pending appeal; special test — must not be in interests of justice.

nodes.label: Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal Ordinance (Cap 484) s.35
Variation / Revocation / Breach of Bail
nodes.summary: Court may vary conditions on application by prosecution or accused. Breach of bail condition: accused may be arrested without warrant (Cap 221 s.9N); new bail hearing required. Anticipated breach: police may apply to court.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.9N
nodes.summary: Breach of bail condition; arrest without warrant and new bail hearing.

nodes.label: Police / ICAC Bail
nodes.summary: Police may grant bail after arrest (Cap 232 s.52(1A)), with conditions; if refused, accused brought to court. ICAC bail similar (Cap 204 s.10A(3)).

nodes.label: Bail Flow: Person Arrested or Charged
nodes.summary: Step 1: Person is arrested or charged with an offence.

nodes.label: Bail Flow: Police/ICAC/Court Route
nodes.summary: Step 2: Determine whether bail route is police, ICAC, or court-based.

nodes.label: Bail Flow: Consider Right to Bail
nodes.summary: Step 3: Apply presumption of right to bail under Cap 221 s.9D(1).

nodes.label: Bail Flow: Refusal Grounds
nodes.summary: Step 4: Check statutory refusal grounds (s.9D(2): absconding, reoffending, witness interference). Check NSL Art.42 if applicable.

nodes.label: Bail Flow: Conditions / Recognizance / Surety
nodes.summary: Step 5: If bail granted, impose proportionate conditions, recognizance, or surety.

nodes.label: Bail Flow: Breach or Anticipated Breach
nodes.summary: Step 6: If conditions breached or breach anticipated, apply for arrest warrant or variation.

nodes.label: Bail Flow: Variation / Revocation / Appeal
nodes.summary: Step 7: Variation or revocation of bail, or appeal against bail decision.
